slides.text: A chatbot reacts. An AI agent acts. The word that matters is autonomy.
slides.voiceover_text: Did you know the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent comes down to just one word? Autonomy.

slides.text: Understands natural language, not a rigid click-through decision tree.
slides.voiceover_text: Tip one: an agent understands natural language, so it doesn't collapse the moment someone goes off the script.

slides.text: Decides what to do using your rules and live data.
slides.voiceover_text: Tip two: it decides what to do using your rules and live data pulled from your systems.

slides.text: Acts on it: books the job, updates your CRM.
slides.voiceover_text: Tip three: then it acts. It books the job and updates your CRM without you touching it.

slides.text: A chatbot follows a script. An agent handles the whole job.
slides.voiceover_text: So remember: a chatbot just follows a script, but a real agent handles the whole job.

youtubeTitle: Chatbot Vs AI Agent: What Makes An Agent
youtubeDescription: A chatbot reacts to a script. An AI agent acts on its own. The difference is autonomy: it understands language, decides using your rules and live data, then completes the job.
geo_answer: An AI agent is software that perceives information, makes decisions and acts autonomously to complete tasks, whereas a chatbot simply follows a fixed script.
geo_takeaways: The key difference between a chatbot and an AI agent is autonomy: a chatbot reacts, an AI agent acts.
AI agents understand natural language, so they handle accents, slang and incomplete sentences far better than older tools.
Without integration to your calendar and CRM, an AI agent is just a clever answering machine.
